neighbours.label: The English verb 'break' (break/breaks/broke/breaking) followed by its object, peaking on the word right after it: 'break the silence', 'break my mug', 'broke the record', 'breaking up the monotony'. Quiet for other verbs with the same object (smash, crack, end, shatter), for the noun 'break' (a lunch break, spring break) and for other languages; 'break' with no object (the glass broke, the car broke down) is only middling.
fire: She finally decided to break the silence at dinner.
Please don't break my favorite mug again.
The sprinter broke the world record in Tokyo.
A short walk helps with breaking up the monotony of the afternoon.
He breaks the eggs into a bowl before whisking them.
The kids broke a window while playing baseball.
Nobody wanted to break the news to the coach.
You should never break a promise to a friend.
quiet: After the divorce he was completely broke.
That lucky bounce was the break the team needed.
She finally decided to end the silence at dinner.
Please don't smash my favorite mug again.
The sprinter set a new world record in Tokyo.
A short walk helps with relieving the monotony of the afternoon.
He cracks the eggs into a bowl before whisking them.
The kids shattered a window while playing baseball.
